checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: One ~8s vertical video shows a fictional adult woman addressing the camera in a home setting
must.why: 8 s 9:16 clips show a woman in her 30s selfie-style in a living room, looking at the camera.

must.item: Complete supplied script audible in English without omissions or added claims
must.why: Audio was not transcribed; the picture only shows she is speaking.

must.item: Readable captions reproduce the script exactly and follow the speech
must.why: The captioned clip shows 'so easy, I finally have a' with a comma where the script has a period. The same caption sits on screen at 3.2 s and 5.6 s, so it looks stuck or out of sync. The final 'routine that sticks' was not seen in the sampled frames, and no caption is visible at 7.6 s.

must.item: Presenter visibly speaks rather than remaining a still image
must.why: Mouth shapes, head and hand positions change across frames, and she smiles at the end.

must.item: Ad does not label the presenter as a verified or real customer
must.why: No such label appears on screen.

exact_text.text: FitTrack makes planning my workouts so easy. I finally have a routine that sticks.
exact_text.read_as: Captions read 'FitTrack makes planning my workouts' then 'so easy, I finally have a'. The period after 'easy' became a comma, and 'routine that sticks' was not seen in the sampled frames.

faults.what: Captions do not match the script exactly: a comma replaces the period after 'easy', and the last words ('routine that sticks') were not seen on screen.
The same caption 'so easy, I finally have a' appears at 3.2 s and 5.6 s, which suggests the captions are out of sync with the speech.
Captions use heavy yellow text with an outline, placed over her face and chest. This is a bold style, not a subtle one.
The assistant said it hadn't watched the video, and it delivered two clips (one captioned, one not).

summary: The video is a convincing 8 s vertical selfie-style testimonial with a speaking, friendly woman, but the captions are altered (comma for period, last words not seen) and look out of sync, so the user would likely ask for a fix.
